newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's Farson group sees profits slip.
newsitem.headline: Malta's Farson group sees profits slip.

text.p: Malta's Simonds Farsons Cisk group said on Wednesday it made a pre-tax profit of 410,000 Maltese pounds ($1.05 million) for the year ended last January 31 against 815,000 pounds for the 10 months up to January 31, 1996.
Turnover was up to 17.6 million, an increase of 15.5 per cent for the year compared to the 10-month period to January 31, 1996.
No year-to-year comparisons could be made because the group changed its financial year in 1996 following listing on the Malta Stock Exchange.
The group, one of Malta's largest, is built around a brewery but is also involved in beverages, a food chain that includes the Pizza Hut, Burger King and KFC franchises, and real estate.

The group said in a statement the results were affected by a slowdown in 1996 of the hotel, pub and restaurant trade, an enforced price reduction in the price of beers, and a price war in the grocery trade as well as start-up costs for some of its franchises.

The board is taking a number of measures to improve the group's profitability in the coming years. including competitive terms to customers, reducing internal cost structures and improving efficiency and expanding the group's restaurant business. ($1=0.38 cents)
